title: Access without changing what is measured
statement: Let no access need block participation, use equivalent access modes only where what is measured stays unchanged, so reading-test passages are never read aloud, and disclose supports that change it.
detail: The review hub's student-course quality standard makes it a universal requirement that access needs neither prevent participation nor change the construct without disclosure, shown by automated checks plus manual keyboard, focus, screen-reader, zoom, contrast, reduced-motion, target-size, audio-fallback and target-device tests on the exact artifact. Its requirement for source-based work lets the complete first encounter with a source use an equivalent access mode when that does not change the construct. Both are requirements of a standard, with no measured outcome behind them.
against: The reference publisher leaves construct policy to states (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_RESPONSE.md`, line 97), so where the line falls can differ from one state's test to another's.

evidence.quote: Access needs do not prevent participation or change the construct without disclosure.
A complete encounter may use an equivalent access mode when that does not change the construct.
TTS on stems/answer choices only — NEVER on reading passages
Passages read aloud measure listening comprehension, not reading (NWEA's own per-part TTS control enforces the same boundary).
TTS available on stems and answer choices, **not on reading passages** (a reading-comprehension score obtained with passages read aloud measures a different construct)
The accommodations note claimed TTS on stems/choices; **the product had none**
